acceptedReports.program: Orange County civil legal aid, medical-legal partnerships and impact litigation

acceptance.evidence: Independent root original-audit and clinical-source challenge plus726 reconstruction checks: docs/geography-discovery/la-public-law-center-root-acceptance-20261005.md. Conditional partial-world reference, not observed effect or verified donor expansion.

what: Public Law Center provides free civil legal assistance to low-income Orange County residents through staff lawyers, clinics and pro bono representation.
Its lawyers address housing, safety, insurance coverage, medical billing and other practical barriers that can threaten health and household stability.
Medical-legal partnerships connect this advocacy with hospitals and family-resource centers, while broader representation helps clients exercise existing rights.
strengths: Insurance appeals and representation offer a concrete route from a legal barrier to otherwise-missed care.
Housing, safety and financial legal work can protect resources as well as health.
Staff-supported volunteer representation and established clinical partnerships provide a substantial delivery platform.
reservations: Approximate case counts do not reveal distinct clients, implemented additional resolutions or net collected household resources.
The clinical and financial conversions are explicitly conditional judgments, not PLC treatment effects imported from external trials.
Ordinary-gift expansion, creditor/public-payer incidence, litigation burdens and wider portfolio effects remain unresolved.

sections.what:
Public Law Center, EIN 95-3709253, is an Orange County pro bono legal-aid recipient. Ordinary support covers direct representation, advice, clinics, nonprofit assistance and impact litigation across many practice areas. Its current homepage reports nearly 3,800 cases and over 75,000 staff/volunteer hours in an unspecified 'last year'; these are approximate scale indicators, not a dated clinical cohort. [Recipient scope](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/)

The AIDS Legal Assistance Project addresses insurance disputes, housing, employment, privacy and estate/family matters for low-income people living with HIV. Not all such work changes medication adherence or survival. [ALAP](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/hiv-aids-legal-assistance/)

Current MLPs include Orange County Health Care Agency, biweekly Hoag clinics and weekly South Orange County family-resource-center clinics. The Health Law Unit handles coverage eligibility, denied services/drugs/equipment, medical review and billing. [Partnerships](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/medical-legal-partnerships/) [Health law](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/health-law/)
sections.monitoring:
The current website describes services and staffing, but the reviewed sources do not provide annual ALAP/health-law unique-client counts, the share initially out of HIV care, coverage retained because of representation, or linked clinical outcomes. A clinic schedule does not identify its patient volume, completed representation or health yield.

Useful monitoring would follow each resolved legal barrier into otherwise-missed treatment, sustained treatment duration, clinical severity, actual household exposure and health change. Legal success without changed care remains a legal outcome; a successful insurance appeal is not automatically the lifetime benefit of treatment. Compare with the help the patient would receive from case managers, hospital advocates, other lawyers and existing programs.

The official-linked volunteer list demonstrates live demand for representation across several legal specialties. It is evidence of potential volunteer matching work, not an audited cash funding gap or an estimate of additional health cases. No private client narrative or identifying detail is reproduced. [Volunteer opportunities](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/case-list/)

Resource monitoring should also record net enforceable collections or benefits after tax and benefit offsets, client time and travel, unique household overlap, creditor/public-payer incidence and the duration of recurring benefits. Raw matters, face-value canceled bills and promotional work valuations are not equivalent to disposable resources.
sections.qualitative:
A Philadelphia feasibility study randomized two service organizations, enrolling 202 people with HIV. The intervention site had higher odds of viral suppression at three months (OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.06–5.49); the six-month estimate was not significant. With only one site in each arm, site-specific care and implementation differences cannot be confidently separated from the intervention. This is encouraging mechanism evidence, not a portable PLC risk reduction or a lifetime treatment effect. [Original study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10461-025-04901-w)

An individually randomized primary-care MLP trial found lower stress and fewer emergency visits but higher anxiety and hospital use. Some additional hospital use may represent appropriate access, rather than harm; nonetheless, the mixed outcomes do not justify a universally positive QALY-per-legal-case assumption. [Original randomized trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)

The START antiretroviral trial establishes a real clinical bridge when treatment actually changes: among initially healthy adults with CD4 counts above 500, serious AIDS/non-AIDS events or death occurred at 1.38 versus 0.60 per 100 person-years with deferred versus immediate treatment. That 0.0078 event-per-person-year difference is not a PLC effect. Current patients, interruption duration, event mix and treatment alternatives may differ substantially. It can anchor a conditional clinical calculation, not establish the local strategy-equivalent exposure produced by legal aid. ART was used during 94% of immediate-arm versus 28% of deferred-arm follow-up, so this difference cannot be multiplied directly by additional ART-years. [Original START paper](https://www.natap.org/2015/IAS/nejmoa15068161.pdf)

Housing stability, safety from abuse, reduced financial distress and equitable legal access may generate substantial benefits outside this HIV branch. Conversely, litigation stress, privacy risks, delay and opportunity costs matter. None is silently assigned zero in a claimed complete portfolio return.

The new central scenario is broader than HIV treatment alone: 25% of the approximate 3,800 annual cases are assumed to involve a potentially material health barrier, including access to care, safe housing or personal safety. The current health-law scope and volunteer case list make these mechanisms plausible, but do not establish that percentage. Of those cases, a 25% incremental implemented-resolution probability is assumed relative to hospital advocates, other lawyers and existing protection. A further 25% funding response discounts grants, reserves and volunteer replacement. These are explicit subjective priors, not observed PLC rates.

A changed case receives a net 0.03 annual survival-adjusted utility gain for two years, then zero. This small finite health area is a judgment about heterogeneous clinical, safety and stress effects, not an effect imported from START or the MLP trials. A 10% deduplication/overlap reduction prevents treating repeated legal matters and shared health improvements as fully independent. One affected person's trajectory per case is counted; no automatic family-size or lifetime multiplier is used. Zero and harm remain plausible. Legal and systemic value outside this health-relevant component is unpriced.
sections.cost:
The newest official-linked audit reports 2025 expense of $22,061,260 plus $163,247 direct event costs netted against revenue: $22,224,507 full annual recognized resources. This includes $12,343,512 contributed legal services; removing them yields $9,880,995 non-donated accrual expense, not cash-only marginal cost. The comparable 2023–2025 full-cost mean is $20,866,597.33. The current audit has an unmodified opinion. [2025 audit](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2025-Public-Law-Center-Financial-Statement.pdf)

The clinical reference remains 3.067531 finite QALYs. Resource exposure is separate: 3,800 matters × .8 unique-household share × .25 funding response = 760 household units, whether or not clinical outcomes improve. Financial relevance .5 and additional implemented resolution .25 imply 95 financial-resolution households. Each receives a judged net one-time $1,500 change, not an observed award or gross avoided bill. After retaining half the positive gain for health overlap and subtracting the full $100 process burden, its net is $650. The other 665 households lose $100. These costs include time, travel and lost work resources; clinical failure does not erase them. One modeled welfare person per household uses a judged $20,000 annual household baseline, one finite year and one-year delay. Household gain and burden are combined before the log.

The shared production bridge yields −0.143180 healthy-year welfare equivalents: .5×[95 log(1+650/20,000)+665 log(1−100/20,000)]/1.03. Added once to clinical health, the conditional partial-boundary total is 2.924351 and the price is $75.998082 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, versus the initial $69.672884 million per ten clinical QALYs. A $10,000 gift-scaled share implies about .001316 combined equivalents only under the proportional annual-work hypothesis; this is not a quoted expansion offer.

Creditor, public-payer and additional clinical-provider incidence is unknown in the central reference, not factual zero. Matched-transfer and partner-cost scenarios explicitly subtract signed disjoint payer resources, including full costs when clinical effects fail. Canceled debt face value is not necessarily recoverable creditor revenue; neither avoided rent nor benefits can be claimed as new world resources without incidence. Nonlocal payer losses, institutional-client burdens and systemic policy effects remain unpriced. Contributed lawyer time is already in full C; no invented foregone volunteer earnings are added again. Two-year financial duration is explicitly a recurrent-benefit hypothesis, not repeated counting of one-time collection. Clinical-null, financial-only, true-zero, adverse and complete-unknown controls are serialized.

The .25 funded-work response retains the full annual cost denominator while judging how much of gross service activity this resource package adds relative to continuing alternatives. It is not a second discount on measured incremental outcomes. A b=1 scenario counts the full modeled annual work response; neither case establishes a marginal donor tranche. The original clinical-only diagnostic remains preserved unchanged.
sections.funding:
The 2025 audit reports $4,631,909 cash and investments, $3,373,519 financial assets available for general expenditure, and $1,796,796 purpose-restricted net assets, including housing and immigration. Unrestricted net assets fell $477,800 while total net assets rose because of restricted contributions. The 2024 single audit remained unfinalized as of year end; potential questioned costs were unknown. These accounting facts do not identify a currently unfunded marginal general-support work plan. [Newest audit](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2025-Public-Law-Center-Financial-Statement.pdf)

Existing grants, volunteer supply, public eligibility and hospital advocates stay in the counterfactual. A two-year supported fellowship is not a new donor-created cohort. Ordinary general support is the modeled recipient scope; staffing, volunteer conversion and alternative financing require donor diligence. [Official donation route](https://publiclawcenter.networkforgood.com/projects/20106-public-law-center-donations)

model.costScope: Full 2025 annual recognized recipient resource package including contributed legal services and event costs. b=.25 is a conditional annual-funded-work response against continuing alternative capacity, not a second donor discount on measured additional outcomes. The denominator remains the entire annual package, not one quarter of cost. b=1 is explicit sensitivity; marginal-gift conversion remains unknown. Outside household/provider incidence is separate signed welfare, not added again to C.
model.geographicAttribution: Direct Orange County household branch inside LA–Long Beach–Anaheim; one welfareperson per household, no family multiplication. Counterparty scenarios assume local disjoint payer units, nonlocal incidence unpriced.
model.formula: Health=g*[positiveOnly(K*e*a*b*q*sum(y=0..T-1)(1+d)^-(healthDelay+y),z)-exposure*harm/(1+d)^healthDelay]. exposure=K*uniqueHH*b; financial=exposure*fShare*fAdditionality. Recipient paths net positiveOnly(resourceGain,positiveOverlap)-processCost before log for financial HH, and -processCost for otherHH. Income=sum .5*people*sum finite discounted log(1+net/baseline)*g. Combined=clinical+income; price10=10*C/Combined only if known and positive.
model.counterfactual: Existing public/hospital care, legal protection, alternative lawyers, volunteer availability and already-supported fellowships continue. a is additional implemented resolution within PLC's gross case cohort, not an extra coalition discount on already-attributed outcomes. b separately measures capacity response to general support.
model.attribution: Approximate all-case count is filtered for health relevance, additional resolution and gift response. z reduces repeated matters/overlapping health. One finite person-level trajectory per changed case. No separate START/HIV credit added to the same insured treatment. The .25 funded-work response is an annual-package counterfactual prior; no actual annual incremental resolution series has already been credited. It is consequential and unverified, not measured marginal donor leverage.
model.uncertainty: Clinical scale/conversion retained as conditional alpha prior. External trials show mixed short-term outcomes, not calibrated PLC QALYs. All resource conversions and counterparty allocation are judgments; complete portfolio unknown remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Conditional reference:950 health-relevant matters,59.375 additionally changed cases,53.4375 positive-overlap-retained clinical trajectories;3.067531 clinicalQALYs. Separately760 incremental distinct resource-exposed client households,95 additionally resource-changing resolutions and665 other exposed households; these are judged expectations, not observed counts.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full annual recognized recipient resource cost including donated legal services and netted event addback. Health-relevant resolution component, not MLP-only expense or full portfolio return. This price includes donated legal services, rather than only dollars a donor must supply; it is not a verified next-dollar cash return.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: g=1 for modeled Orange County direct-client health, within LA/Orange. Wider litigation spillovers not counted.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: A(T)=sum(y=1..T)(1.03^-y). QLA=K*e*a*b*q*A(T)*z*g. K=3800,e=.25,a=.25,b=.25,q=.03,T=2,z=.9,g=1 => QLA=3.067531105665. Price10=10*21372374/QLA. Qportfolio=QLA+Qother-H; other non-overlapping health unknown.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Existing public/hospital care, legal protection, alternative lawyers, volunteer availability and already-supported fellowships continue. a is additional implemented resolution within PLC's gross case cohort, not an extra coalition discount on already-attributed outcomes. b separately measures capacity response to general support.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: Approximate all-case count is filtered for health relevance, additional resolution and gift response. z reduces repeated matters/overlapping health. One finite person-level trajectory per changed case. No separate START/HIV credit added to the same insured treatment.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Subjective best estimate of a broad legal-health component. Case mix, additional resolutions and utility are not measured or source-calibrated local probabilities. Trials motivate plausibility and caution, not numerical transfer. Zero/harm and wide joint cases retained.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: 3800*.25=950 potentially health-relevant cases; *.25 resolution increment *.25 funding response=59.375 expected changed cases; *.9 overlap factor=53.4375. Each carries .03 utility for two discounted years. Fractional cases are expectations, not observed case outcomes.
